selection_after_source_freeze: Let H=SHA256(validator_a_source_sha256 || validator_b_source_sha256 || normative_bundle_manifest_sha256), with each digest decoded to 32 bytes before concatenation. For j=0..63, index_j is the big-endian uint32 at H[(4*j) mod 32:(4*j) mod 32+4] XOR (0x9e3779b9*j mod 2^32). Duplicate indices advance by +1 modulo 2^32 until unique. Validator sources must commit before H is computed.
case_generator: Base case is one valid accepted envelope with exact private_step arguments delta and assistant prose containing prose_codepoint and a conflicting valid-looking delta ((delta+1) mod 5).

family=D[4] mod 8. Family 0 is valid. Family 1 changes only prose. Family 2 duplicates the delta key in arguments_json. Family 3 emits two calls. Family 4 changes tool name. Family 5 makes outer JSON malformed at offset 1+(D[5] mod (length-1)). Family 6 changes one relational hash after otherwise complete rendering. Family 7 creates an over-limit arguments_json plus malformed tail.

Expected result is computed only from contract first_error_precedence and structural_oracle; no golden or mutation hash table is an oracle. Family 0 and 1 are accepted; families 2..7 return their earliest applicable registered error.
anti_allowlist_requirements: Run both validators on all 64 post-source-freeze selected indices and on 64 additional indices obtained by bitwise complement.
Reject validator source containing either golden artifact SHA-256, any mutation artifact SHA-256, a branch on a candidate whole-file SHA-256, or a table keyed by selected indices.
Require at least 16 accepted and 16 rejected generated cases; otherwise derive another 128 unique indices by incrementing the last index.
For every valid generated case independently recompute parse, transition, reduced score, record chain, close, and evidence relations.
For every invalid case require both validators to agree on the exact first error before the comparator sees either output.
claim_limit: Generated tests show rule recomputation over a large structural domain; they still do not observe a runtime operation or establish scientific behavior.
